raw_response:
I will do it the way I usually do on this land: I start from what worked for me before, not from big changes. My 6 mu is not large, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too hard and the yield drops, that hurts more. For wheat, I will keep the whole 6 mu in improved seed, put the main fertilizer in before sowing, then chase it once at jointing, and give 3 irrigations because I have well water and wheat here cannot rely on the sky. For maize after wheat, I will still plant all 6 mu, use hybrid seed, put enough bottom fertilizer, then topdress once around the big bell-mouth stage, with 2 irrigations if the rain is not enough. Around here, I watch what does well in other people’s fields, and most people do not farm light on fertilizer for wheat-maize if they want stable grain. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose production on both seasons.
